$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$bytes = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("$env:TEMP\opencode\opencode_copy.db")
$text = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($bytes)
$sid = 'ses_f4e508695ffeguNWxcKifyQgHS'

# Fast role map: message records (single-shot regex)
$roleRx = [regex]::new('"id":"(msg_[^"]*)","sessionID":"' + $sid + '"((?:[^"]*"[^"]*")*?)"role":"([^"]*)"')
$roleById = @{}
foreach ($m in $roleRx.Matches($text)) { if (-not $roleById.ContainsKey($m.Groups[1].Value)) { $roleById[$m.Groups[1].Value] = $m.Groups[3].Value } }

# Fast part extraction
$partRx = [regex]::new('"id":"prt_[^"]*","sessionID":"' + $sid + '","messageID":"(msg_[^"]*)","type":"(text|reasoning|summary)","text":"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"')
$rows = @()
foreach ($m in $partRx.Matches($text)) {
    $after = $text.Substring($m.Index + $m.Length, [Math]::Min(40, $text.Length - ($m.Index + $m.Length)))
    $tm = [regex]::Match($after, '"time":(\d+)')
    $t = 0
    if ($tm.Success) { $t = [long]$tm.Groups[1].Value }
    $txt = [regex]::Replace($m.Groups[3].Value, '\\u([0-9a-fA-F]{4})', { param($mm) [char][int]('0x' + $mm.Groups[1].Value) })
    $rows += , [pscustomobject]@{ Time=$t; Msg=$m.Groups[1].Value; Type=$m.Groups[2].Value; Text=$txt }
}
$rows = $rows | Sort-Object Time

$sb = New-Object System.Text.StringBuilder
foreach ($r in $rows) {
    $d = if ($r.Time) { ([DateTimeOffset]::FromUnixTimeMilliseconds($r.Time).ToLocalTime().ToString('yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss')) } else { '????-' }
    $who = if ($roleById[$r.Msg]) { $roleById[$r.Msg] } else { '?' }
    [void]$sb.AppendLine("[$d] role=$who type=$($r.Type)")
    $clean = ($r.Text -replace '\\n', ' ') -replace '\\r', ' ' -replace '\\"', '"'
    [void]$sb.AppendLine($clean)
    [void]$sb.AppendLine('========================================')
}
$out = $sb.ToString()
[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText("$env:TEMP\opencode\arsheef_full_session.txt", $out, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))
"roles found: $($roleById.Count)"
"parts: $($rows.Count)"
"out bytes: $([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("$env:TEMP\opencode\arsheef_full_session.txt").Length)"

733: اكتملت ميزات الذكاء الاصطناعي الأربع والبناء.\n\n**آخر ما أُنجز في هذه الجلسة:**\n- أنشأت `work/AiAnalysisScheduler.kt` وربطته في `FileScannerWorker` بعد الفحص، وفي `AddFab` بعد الإضافة اليدوية، وفي `ArsheefApplication` عند بدء التطبيق.\n- أصلحت واجهة ML Kit: العيون عبر `getLandmark(FaceLandmark.LEFT_EYE)` بدل الدوال غير الموجودة (`FaceGroupingEngine.kt:74`).\n- أصلحت خللًا حقيقيًا: `hashToHex` كان يستخدم `Long.toString(16)` فيعطي بادئة `-` للقيم السالبة ويكسر `parseUnsignedLong` — استبدلته بـ `java.lang.Long.toUnsignedString(...)`.\n- الواجهات: `AiPanelContent` في القائمة الجانبية، شاشة `FacesScreen` + مسار `Screen.Faces`، شارات الوسوم ومقتطف OCR في العارض، واقتراحات `rememberScopeSuggestions` في نوافذ التسمية بسنة/شهر/يوم.\n\n**النتيجة:**\n- الترجمة نظيفة بلا أخطاء ولا تحذيرات.\n- اختبارات الوحدة: **٢٣ ناجحًا** (٩ قائمة + ٦ بصمة + ٨ اقتراحات).\n- `assembleDebug` نجح → `app\\build\\outputs\\apk\\debug\\app-debug.apk` (54.2 MB).\n\nملاحظة محيطية باقية: OCR يعمل فعليًا على Android 13+ فقط عبر انعكاس `TextRecognizer`، وسيُتخطى بهدوء على ما دونه.

741: [2026-09-18 06:12:02] role=? msg=?
742: الذكاء الاصطناعي في المشروع كله **يعمل على الجهاز بلا إنترنت** ولا يرفع أي صورة، ويتكوّن من أربع ميزات:\n\n**١. التصنيف التلقائي** — `ai/SmartClassifier.kt`\nيحلل الصورة (سطوع/تشبع/حواف) ويضع وسومًا مثل: مستند، لقطة شاشة، طبيعة، سماء/ماء، أبيض وأسود، إضاءة منخفضة، صور أشخاص. الوسوم تُخزَّن في `image_labels`.\n\n**٢. استخراج النصوص (OCR)** — `ai/OcrEngine.kt`\nيستخرج النص العربي/الإنجليزي من الصور والمستندات عبر نموذج النظام `android.graphics.text.TextRecognizer` (Android 13+). يُخزَّن في `ocr_texts` ويصبح قابلاً للبحث ضمن البحث الشامل (`ArchivedImageDao.searchAll`).\n\n**٣. تجميع الوجوه** — `ai/FaceGroupingEngine.kt`\nيكتشف الوجوه بـ ML Kit، يحاذيها بالعينين، يقصّها إلى ٦٤×٦٤، ثم يحسب بصمة `dHash` (٦٤ بت). الوجوه المتشابهة (مسافة هامنغ ≤ 10) تُجمع في شخص واحد (`face_groups` / `face_group_members`)، مع حفظ صور الوجوه المقصوصة كأغلفة.\n\n**٤. اقتراح أسماء ذكية** — `ai/NameSuggester.kt`\nمن نصوص OCR + الوسوم + أسماء مجموعات الوجوه يولّد اقتراحات عربية عند التسمية المخصصة (مثل: \"وثائق عقود\"، \"فواتير\"، \"صور أحمد\") تظهر كرقائق قابلة للنقر في نافذة التسمية.\n\n**كيف يعمل خلف الكواليس:** `work/AiAnalysisWorker.kt` يدفع المعالجة على دفعات (١٢٠ صورة/تشغيل)، يُطلق تلقائيًا بعد فحص الاستيراد، وعند فتح التطبيق، وبعد الإضافة اليدوية. كل صورة تُعلَّم بـ `aiAnalyzedAt` فلا تُعاد معالجتها. تتحكم بالميزات من لوحة \"الذكاء الاصطناعي\" في القائمة الجانبية مع زر إعادة تحليل كامل.\n\n**الفائدة العملية:** البحث يشمل الكلمات داخل الصور والأسماء، والأرشيف يتنظم بصريًا، والتسمية تصبح أسرع، والوجوه تُجمع دون رفع أي شيء لأي خدمة خارجية.

805: اكتملت المراجعة — **4 خلل تعمل الآن، والباقي اتضح سليمًا**.\n\n**أُصلح (شرح لكل منها):**\n\n1. **تكرار الوجوه عند إعادة التحليل** — `resetAiAnalysis` لم يمسح `face_group_members`، فكانت تنمو بأبناء مكررة. الآن `AiAnalysisWorker` يستدعي `purgeFaceDataForImage` (تحذف الأعضاء + ملفات القص) قبل إعادة إدراج الوجه، ولا يمسح أسماء المجموعات اليدوية. النتيجة: إعادة التحليل Idempotent ويُبقي المجموعات المسماة مستقرة.\n2. **أشباح البيانات عند حذف صور/سنوات/أيام** — `deleteImages`/`deleteYear`/`deleteMonth`/`deleteDay` لم تنظف OCR والوسوم والأعضاء فكانت تكدّس صفوفًا تتعلق بصور محذوفة (وكلف ملفات قص على القرص) ويظهر عدد مجموعات وهمي. أضفت `cleanupAiRowsForImages` (مع تقسيم 400-دفعات حمايةً من حد SQLite البالغ 999 متغيرًا).\n3. **تسريب `TextRecognizer`** — كان يُنشأ ولا يُغلق (يبقي نموذج النص مثبتًا بالذاكرة). أضفت `closeInstance` عبر الانعكاس في `isAvailable` و`recognizeFile` معًا.\n4. **كشف الوجه مرتين لكل صورة** — الآن تمريرة واحدة، نتيجتها تُستخدم للإشارة في التصنيف وللتجميع معًا.\n\n**مؤكد سليم عند المراجعة:**\n- `MIGRATION_3_4` يطابق الكيانات نوعًا ونوعًا (نص/indexes)، والجداول جديدة فلا يمسّ البيانات القائمة.\n- `searchAll` معاملة parameterized؛ الاستعلامات لا تسرّب الصفوف اليتيمة.\n- عارض الوجه ومواضع العينين كلاهما في فضاء `MAX_DETECT_DIMENSION=1024` نفسه → المحاذاة والتوجيه متوافقان.\n- حسابات `SmartClassifier` محمية (لا قسمة على صفر، `decodeSampled` يرجع null بأمان)، وكل bitmaps تُعاد تدويرها.\n- تتابع العمل لا يسمح بتشغيلين متداخلين (APPEND_OR_REPLACE يصفّفُهما سلسلة).\n\n**النتيجة:** `compileDebugKotlin` بلا أخطاء ولا تحذيرات، اختبارات الوحدة **23/23**، و`assembleDebug` ناجح.\n\n**تحفظان واقعيان (ليست أخطاء):**\n- OCR يعمل فعليًا على Android 13+ ويعتمد على توفر نموذج اللغة على جهاز المستخدم.\n- تجميع الوجوه تعميم إحصائي (dHash + هامينغ ≤ 10) — دقيق في الزوايا/الإضاءة المتقاربة، وقد يحتاج دمج/تقسيم يدويًا للقِطع الصعبة.

package com.alarsheef.archive.data.entities

import androidx.room.Entity
import androidx.room.Index
import androidx.room.PrimaryKey

enum class SourceApp { WHATSAPP, GALLERY, DOWNLOADS, MANUAL_CAMERA, MANUAL_IMPORT }

/**
 * كل عنصر بالأرشيف صورة — حتى لو أصله PDF (يتحوّل لصورة/صور وقت الاستيراد).
 * contentHash: بصمة رقمية (SHA-256) لمحتوى الصورة الفعلي، تُستخدم لاكتشاف التكرار
 * عبر كامل الأرشيف بدل الاعتماد على اسم أو مسار الملف فقط.
 * receivedCount: يُزاد فقط عند وصول نفس الصورة يدويًا مرة ثانية (لا يزيد من الفحص التلقائي).
 */
@Entity(
    tableName = "archived_images",
    indices = [
        Index(value = ["contentHash"], unique = true),
        Index(value = ["year", "month", "day"]),
        Index(value = ["originalPath"])
    ]
)
data class ArchivedImage(
    @PrimaryKey(autoGenerate = true)
    val id: Long = 0,

    val fileName: String,
    val storedPath: String,
    val contentHash: String,
    val sourceApp: SourceApp,
    val receivedCount: Int = 1,

    val year: Int,
    val month: Int,
    val day: Int,

    val importedAt: Long,
    val capturedAt: Long,

    /**
     * المسار الأصلي للملف في مصدره (واتساب/استديو/تنزيلات/مجلد مخصص).
     * يُعبَّأ فقط لملفات الفحص التلقائي الثابتة؛ يبقى فارغًا للإضافة اليدوية
     * وصفحات PDF المؤقتة وملفات الاستعادة من ZIP.
     * يمنع تضخّم عدّاد "مرات الاستلام": أي ملف بنفس المسار يُتجاهل كليةً
     * في الفحص اليومي دون إعادة حساب بصمته أو زيادة العدّاد.
     */
    val originalPath: String? = null,

    /**
     * وقت اكتمال التحليل الذكي (OCR + تصنيف + وجوه) لهذه الصورة.
     * null يعني أنه لم يُحلَّل بعد؛ يُستخدم لمعالجة الواردات الجديدة فقط
     * دون إعادة تحليل الأرشيف كله كل يوم.
     */
    val aiAnalyzedAt: Long? = null
)

The searches found nothing (no jdk dirs, no .gradle\jdks matches; the previous output shows mixed results — Android Studio jbr only). Let me search more broadly:
- `C:\Program Files\Microsoft\jdk*`
- Windows "Program Files" matched empty because my Where filter didn't find. Hmm the last command's output was a list of directories but they look like entries from where jdk|jbr... wait output shows 20 blank-ish lines then nothing; those were actually directory names of C:\Program Files etc but where clause filtered on name — the blank lines might be the FullName list got mangled (encoding of names?). It printed many empty lines — odd. Possibly FullName with non-ASCII names shown blank due to encoding.

Let me do a targeted search for java.exe across likely locations: C:\Program Files (jbr only?), and check for microsoft jdk, temurin; also check `C:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr` is JDK 25. Also check `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk\sources` no. Also gradle toolchain: maybe the old build ran through Android Studio IDE which uses... it'd still need a JDK for Gradle. 

Wait — maybe the old session's build happened when Android Studio's JBR was JDK 21 (they may have updated Android Studio recently, which could have upgraded embedded JBR 17→21→25). That would explain "BUILD SUCCESSFUL" earlier but failure now.

Options:
1. Find another JDK. Search C:\ for java.exe may take long. Let me search likely dirs.
2. Download a JDK? Offline constraint — no internet for the machine? Actually web access exists for the assistant (websearch/webfetch), but does the machine have internet? Unknown. Earlier we relied on gradle offline mode + cached deps, suggesting no internet or slow. But we could try downloading a standalone JDK 17 from an Adoptium mirror via the shell. That may fail if no internet. We can test connectivity quickly.
3. Configure Gradle to run Kotlin DSL compiler in-process strategy — already set (kotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process). The failure is the embedded Kotlin script compiler on JDK 25.

Actually, maybe simpler: use a NEWER Gradle that supports Java 25? That would need downloading gradle-8.9+/9.x — needs internet.

Let me first probe internet connectivity and search for other JDKs in parallel.

Actually, wait: there might be JDK inside Android SDK? No. Android Studio has its own JBR only. Check other Android Studio installs? Only one.

Let me search more thoroughly for java.exe on C:\Users and C:\Program Files (limited depth) and simultaneously test internet by trying to download JDK from adoptium via Invoke-WebRequest (small check).

2. Test internet with a HEAD request to https://api.adoptium.net or github.com.

The process was killed again — this time it says "ChildProcess.kill". This is strange. It might be that gradle-wrapper daemon fork + the tool wrapper is having trouble with long-running child processes spawning (gradlew.bat spawns java.exe which spawns a daemon). Or the previous gradle command's daemon is still hanging around (a stale gradle daemon from JDK 25 failed attempt that's wedged), causing the wrapper to hang or exit weirdly.

Actually "ChildProcess.kill" suggests the tool forcibly killed the command, perhaps due to the earlier crashed daemon lingering and holding locks. Also `--offline` may fail if it needs to resolve something and the daemon hangs. Let me check the log file that should have been written (it was written by `*>` redirection — but redirection happens in PowerShell, the log may exist).

Let me:
1. Check the log file tail.
2. Kill any stale gradle daemons (`gradlew --stop` won't run without java; use `Get-Process java | Stop-Process`).
3. Try again with the newer jbr-21 (still ≤22? Java 21 supports up to Gradle 8.7 — Gradle 8.7 supports Java 21). Actually maybe better to use jbr-21.0.11. But first, the log.

Also possible cause: the `*>` redirect of a long build with a bug. Or invocation via `-NonInteractive` PowerShell: gradlelw.bat might prompt? No.

Let me check log and processes.

The `-ArgumentList $Args` fails because `$Args` is the automatic variable in PowerShell (an array of script's own arguments!) — I shadowed it. `$Args` is a built-in automatic variable in a script/function scope. In my function I used `$Args` as parameter name which conflicts. Rename to `$ArgArray`.

Also empty string arguments in ArgumentList cause "element contains null"? No, empty strings are fine. The problem was `$Args` being special — Start-Process got null.

Let me fix: rename param to $ArgArray.

Also note `-ArgumentList $ArgArray` with `@('shell','am','force-stop','com.alarsheef.archive')` — passing arrays splits fine.

Two bugs remain:

1. When calling the script with `param($A1, ...)` — I pass arguments positionally to `am`: `qa.ps1 am force-stop com.alarsheef.archive`. But looking at my script: `"am" { $r = Run-Adb @('shell','am', $A1, $A2, $A3, $A4) }`. Wait the failure says "The argument is null or empty". That means `$ArgArray` contains null entries. In `am` case: `@('shell','am', $A1, $A2, $A3, $A4)` — with A3 and A4 empty strings, that's fine (not null). Hmm but error says "argument is null or empty". Possibly `$ArgArray` parameter binding: calling `Run-Adb @('shell',...)` — fine.

Wait, actually the error arises even at `@('shell','am','force-stop',...)`. But the issue may be that Start-Process -ArgumentList with empty-string entries is rejected! Yes: Start-Process's ArgumentList rejects empty string elements ("argument is null or empty"). A3="" and A4="" are empty strings → error. So I must not pass empty strings to Start-Process.

Fix: filter out empty/null entries in Run-Adb: `$ArgArray = $ArgArray | Where-Object { $_ -ne "" -and $_ -ne $null }`.

2. The dump output has encoding garbled: Arabic shows as "�隩���" — the utf8 file is read by my tool but the console output through bash shows mojibake. The dump worked (EditText = search field, top buttons). The mojibake is because Get-Content -Raw → Write-Output to console which bash tool reads with wrong codepage. For readability, the important thing is the **dump_txt file** content with UTF8. Actually I wrote `Set-Content -Path $dumpTxt -Value $lines -Encoding UTF8`. The tool output shows mojibake but the file should be fine UTF8. I read files with Read tool which handles UTF8. So for dump, better to just confirm exit and I read the file via Read tool.

Two things:
1. `pm list packages` shows `com.alarsheef.archive` IS installed. Good.
2. `sh am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity` → "No intent supplied"! The `-n` got stripped. Why? Because in my `sh` action I do: `$cmd = @($A1, $A2, $A3, $A4) -join ' '`. But adb `shell` with args — `Run-Adb @('shell', $cmd)` where $cmd is a single string. Start-Process -ArgumentList @('shell', 'am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity') passes as two args to adb: "shell" and the rest joined. That should work — `adb shell "am start -n ..."`. But error "No intent supplied" means adb shell received the command but `-n` was consumed... 

Actually the problem: Start-Process -ArgumentList does NOT quote arguments! When ArgumentList contains `@('shell', 'am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity')`, it passes them to adb.exe as raw command-line args without quotes: `adb shell am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity` — since there's no quoting, adb sees multiple args: shell, am, start, -n, com... That should ALSO normally work for `am start -n`! So why "No intent supplied"?

Hmm wait — but the previous run `am start -n ...` also returned 255 with empty output (the "am" action → Run-Adb @('shell','am','start','-n',...)). Am action splits arglists as separate element - each element becomes separate arg: `shell am start -n com..."`. That's equivalent to the above. Both fail with... "No intent supplied"? Actually the "am" action failure earlier printed empty output; we didn't see stderr because my old code printed only $r[1]. Now via sh we see the full error: `IllegalArgumentException: No intent supplied`.

"No intent supplied" for `am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity` — this happens when `am` doesn't see `-n`. WHY would adb eat the `-n`?

AH. I know! In the "sh" path: argument `-n` was in a single string joined, but adb.exe is a Windows program with Windows argument parsing. When Start-Process passes `-ArgumentList @('shell', 'am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity')`, PowerShell constructs the command line. An argument containing a space gets quoted IF PowerShell decides to. Start-Process DOES quote arguments containing spaces when building the process command line (it adds quotes). So adb gets: `shell "am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity"`. adb parses shell args, then sends to device shell: `am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity`. That SHOULD work.

Then why "No intent supplied"? Unless adb (Windows) receives `am` `start` `-n` `com...` as separate args (no quoting) and adb joins them fine too.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider: maybe the Windows command line had quotes stripped or mangled. But the "am" action (separate args, no spaces) ALSO failed earlier with 255 and empty output. Did it give the same "No intent supplied"? Let me test the "am" action again now — it uses Run-Adb @('shell','am','start','-n',...). Each element no spaces, no quoting needed. adb CMD: `adb shell am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity`. adb builds shell command string "am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity", sends to device. Device shell runs am → should work.

But BOTH approaches returned 255. And earlier (in the prior session), `am start` DID work when I ran a raw one-liner. Actually did I? Per summar-notes: "launched via adb shell am start -n..." worked. Which command shape? It was likely a direct one-liner with `-FilePath $adb -ArgumentList @('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity')`. Hmm same shape.

Wait, maybe the issue is **adb shell quoting on the DEVICE side**: `-n` passed literally AND ALSO... "No intent supplied" is from Android Intent.parseCommandArgs. It's thrown when parseCommandArgs sees no non-option components. `-n` should be a valid option. parseCommandArgs handles "-n <component>". Hmm.

Unless the argument arrived as `-n` followed by EMPTY string → "No intent supplied"? When did `-n` get detached from its value? In the "sh" case: `$cmd = @($A1,$A2,$A3,$A4) -join ' '`. But when bash tool calls `powershell -File qa.ps1 sh am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity`, PowerShell -File binding: does `-n` get treated as a switch-like parameter on qa.ps1?! qa.ps1 params are Action, A1..A4 (PositionalArgument). `-n` looks like a parameter name (starts with `-`)! When PowerShell binds `-File` script args, tokens starting with `-` that match a parameter name are treated as parameters; unmatched ones → errors like "-n is not a recognized parameter". But we DIDN'T get binding errors in the "am"/"sh" runs. Hmm, but for the "am" action earlier we DID get: `Parameter cannot be processed because the parameter name 'a' is ambiguous` for `-a`. So `-n` would also be treated as parameter name... but qa.ps1 has no `-n` param → normally errors "'-n' is not a recognized parameter". 

Wait in the "am" run that returned 255 (first one), A1="start", A2="-n", A3="com..." — did it bind "start" to -Action? No, Action="am" was first positional. Positionals $A1,$A2... "start","-n",... then "-n" as parameter-like token — since no parameter named n, PowerShell would error "'n' is not a recognized..." maybe not shown because captured. Actually PowerShell 5.1: for -File invocation, args are passed literally (not parsed as parameters!) — NO, `-File` passes args as-is WITHOUT parameter binding semantics!! `-File` runs the script and passes remaining args as COMMAND ARGUMENTS (bound to param() positionally). PowerShell's `-File` does NOT interpret the script's own args as its parameters. So `-n` etc pass through fine. OK so binding is fine.

So both am and sh with `-n ...` returned 255 "No intent supplied". Yet in the earlier session, `am start -n` worked. What's DIFFERENT? 

OH WAIT. I bet it's the **`-n` in Start-Process -ArgumentList**: `-ArgumentList @('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity')` — Start-Process may interpret... no, ArgumentList elements are literal.

Hmm, but the error is on the DEVICE (adb log shows Java exception from Android). So the shell command reached the device but `am` parsed "start -n com... " and said No intent supplied. That means `am` received `start` but then `-n` didn't parse? parseCommandArgs fails "No intent supplied" only if there are no intent options AND no uri/data. If `-n com...` were present it would parse fine.

Is it possible the DEVICE's toybox sh swallowed `-n`?? No.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider how adb passes shell args. `adb shell cmd1 arg1 arg2 ...` → adb joins args with spaces and runs on device. Standard. `-n` preserved. Should work.

BUT: on some Windows configurations, the command line reaching adb.exe might have the `/` or `-` issue: Windows treats `-n` fine.

Let me test empirically with a DIFFERENT, simpler am invocation that avoids `-n` entirely: `am start -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER -p com.alarsheef.archive` — but that uses `-a` which triggers "am ambiguous param" in qa.ps1 because... no wait, `-File` passes args literally!! But we SAW "'a' is ambiguous" error when I used `-a`! The error said "Parameter cannot be processed because the parameter name 'a' is ambiguous. Possible matches include: -Action -A1 -A2 -A3 -A4." — at qa.ps1. So `-File` DID try to bind `-a` → meaning PowerShell -File DOES parse args as parameters! My assumption was wrong.

So `-n` passed to `powerShell -File qa.ps1` gets interpreted as a PARAMETER of qa.ps1 → but no `-n` param → "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'n'"? We didn't see that error because... hmm, for `am` action run: args were `am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity`. PowerShell -File binds: Action="am", A1="start", then `-n` → param parsing → "n" not a parameter → ERROR (unbound), so `-n` and following "com..." DON'T bind → A2 = ""! That's why adb got `shell am start` with no intent → "No intent supplied"! 

And the `-a` case: "am" ambiguous error → everything after fails (am start even errored).

So the fix: when calling qa.ps1 from bash AND the args contain dashes for the DEVICE, PowerShell -File will choke on params that LOOK like qa.ps1 parameters only if they match/are ambiguous; unknown ones like `-n` → "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'n'" error → arg dropped. To pass literal dashed args, need `--%` or quote with `--`, or use `-Command` with invocation operator `& 'path' args...` (the operator-form passes literals!). Earlier my `-Command "& '$env:TEMP...qa.ps1' key 3"` worked and `tap 220 2400` worked (no dashes). For dashed args, use `-Command` with `& ` invocation → literals preserved!

So the fix: in the bash tool, always invoke via `powershell -Command "& 'qa.ps1' <args>"` instead of `-File`. With `&` operator, args are positional literal strings (not parsed as params). The earlier `-Command "& '...qa.ps1' key 3"` run worked and printed key 3 exit=0 (again $p... errors were from tap/key before my refactor? no - that -Command run output "key 3 exit=" was before refactor, still errored. Whatever, refactor fixed).

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& '$env:TEMP\opencode\qa.ps1' am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity"

$env:TEMP expands inside double-quoted -Command string (PowerShell expands when parsing). Arg `-n` after & operator → literal.

In bash tool direct: `$adb = "..."; & $adb shell am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity` — works.
In qa.ps1 sh: `& $adb @ArgArray` where ArgArray = @('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity')

Both should be identical... unless `@ArgArray` splatting mangles `-n`! PowerShell splatting of an array `@ArgArray` passes each element as a single argument — this is the standard way and preserves dashes. Hmm.

WAIT. Splatting an array DOES pass `-n` as literal. But there's a subtlety: when splatting, PowerShell ALSO parses!! Actually NO — array splatting `@args` passes arguments positionally as literals, NOT as parameters. That's the documented behavior.

But wait, the actual am action ALSO failed earlier even via direct... no, direct worked. Let me look at what qa.ps1 am action passes: Run-Adb @('shell', 'am', 'start', '-n', 'com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'). Same as sh essentially.

Hold on: the difference between my working direct test and qa.ps1: in the direct test I wrote the command inline in the bash tool PowerShell. `& $adb shell am start -n com...` — here `-n` was typed as a LITERAL argument on the command line within a script block (bash tool dispatches whole thing to powershell -Command), NOT inside a -File script. Inside powershell.exe -Command with `& $adb shell am start -n ...`, the `-n` is a native argument — passed literally. Works.

Inside qa.ps1 script file: `& $adb @ArgArray` where ArgArray elements include '-n'. Array-splatt to native command should preserve. Let me TRUST but verify empirically: maybe the bug is that `pm clear` + immediate relaunch — after pm clear, the FIRST `am start` has a race and also the "No intent supplied" is weird.

Hmm wait, actually — look closely: "No intent supplied" AGAIN. This happened with BOTH the Start-Process version AND direct `&` version when invoked FROM qa.ps1. But direct inline works. What's different between inline-at-bash-tool and inside-qa.ps1?

In inline, all args are literal tokens: `shell am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity`. adb gets argv: shell, am, start, -n, com...

In qa.ps1: ArgArray = @('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'). Identical argv...

UNLESS something about `@ArgArray` splatting with the `-n`... known PowerShell gotcha: **splatting array to a native command and `-n`... no.**

Let me actually TEST: add a debug action or run qa.ps1 with echo. Simplest: modify qa.ps1 sh to ALSO print the argv. Actually easier: test directly within a -File-like context: run powershell -Command with the same splat pattern:

powershell -Command "$a=@('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'); $adb='...adb.exe'; & $adb @a"

If THAT fails too, it's the splat that breaks -n. Very plausible actually! I now recall: **`@array` splatting TO NATIVE commands in PowerShell 5.1 passes the elements literally** — but there IS a known bug where splatted arguments that begin with `-` are interpreted... no, that's for functions/cmdlets, not native. For native commands splatting always works literally.

Hmm, but empirically it failed inside qa.ps1. Actually wait — did it? The sh exit=255 error came BEFORE the dump; let me check: is it possible the `pm clear` put the app in "force-stopped" state, and a launch attempt immediately after returns "Warning: ... " no. The ERROR is "No intent supplied" — consistent Intent parsing error, not force-stop.

The splat pattern works fine directly! So the difference is elsewhere. Both work inline. But inside qa.ps1 it fails.

Wait — difference: in qa.ps1, the `sh` action does: `$cmd = @($A1, $A2, $A3, $A4) -join ' '`; Run-Adb @('shell', $cmd). So ArgArray = @('shell','am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'). adb gets 2 args: 'shell' and the full command string. `& $adb shell "am start -n ..."` — PowerShell passes the string as ONE argument (it's one string variable). adb.exe Windows command-line: it must QUOTE it to keep it one arg → `shell "am start -n ..."`. adb then splits the payload by spaces to send to device: "am","start","-n","com..." — should be fine...

BUT WAIT: the "am" ACTION (not sh) also failed the same way. The am action: Run-Adb @('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity') — separate elements. That's the EXACT same as my working direct test! Yet inside qa.ps1 it failed.

So what's different between qa.ps1 environment and inline?

OH WAIT. I see it now!!! In qa.ps1 the script file was EDITED by me. But look at the LAST error message path: `At C:\Users\Me\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\qa.ps1:15` — line 15 is `$out = & $adb @ArgArray 2>&1 | Out-String`. The error is "NativeCommandError". But note in the OUTPUT, the am start error printed even though action was 'am' — no wait, in the LAST run I used 'sh' action. The 'sh' passes SINGLE command string. The DIRECT test I just ran used array elements. Let me test the 'sh'-style single-string form directly!

`$cmd='am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'; & $adb shell $cmd` — the string contains spaces; PowerShell passes it as ONE argv to adb. adb (Windows) receives `shell am start -n ...` as separate argv items (since it's a single argv containing spaces, the Windows process command-line reconstruct requires quoting). adb's arg parsing on Windows: uses its own CommandLineToArgvW → `shell` and `am start -n com...` (the space-containing argv element). Then adb joins args[1:] → "am start -n com..." → device. Works normally.

BUT maybe not — if adb joins correctly it works. Let me just test this exact form.

parts.text:
Both forms work fine directly! So the `qa.ps1` script invocation itself must be the problem. The difference now must be in HOW qa.ps1 is being invoked from the bash tool.

The bash tool calls: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "& '$env:TEMP\opencode\qa.ps1' am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity"`.

Hmm!!! When `& '$env:TEMP\opencode\qa.ps1' am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity` runs: `&` invokes the SCRIPT. `am` → binds to `$Action` positionally. `start` → $A1. Then `-n` → PowerShell tries to bind as a PARAMETER (for script parameters!). `-n` matches nothing → PowerShell actually treats unconsumed `-n` AND its value (because `-n` parse fails, does it swallow next token?) → ERROR "A parameter cannot be found that matches parameter name 'n'. Verify the parameter type and try again." → the whole invocation FAILS with that error, OR `-n` is dropped and `com...` becomes $A2.

We saw neither a "-n param" error NOR "am exit" for the sh run — we saw "sh exit=255" with the Java NoIntent error. So `-n` wasn't consumed by PS binding here...? 

Wait, the sh action's command was: `& 'qa.ps1' sh am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity`. Binding: Action=sh, A1=am, A2=start, then `-n`... if PS tried param binding for `-n`: no such param → writes error & stops? But we got "sh exit=255" meaning the script RAN with A1=am A2=start A3?="" A4?="". So the `-n com.alarsheef...` args got DROPPED silently without error. That means `-c` (continue) semantics: PowerShell treats `-n`... hmm, actually for UNKNOWN `-name` in script invocation with `&`, PowerShell raises an error "A parameter cannot be found..." but continues? It binds subsequent `com...` as positional?? 

Whatever the precise mechanism: `-n` (and compatibly `-a` error we saw) is the problem because **the comma `-n` inside `& 'script.ps1' args` triggers script parameter parsing**.

The AM action directly: `& 'qa.ps1' am start -n com...`. Binding: Action=am... `-n` → PROBLEM SAME. So the am action ALSO got -n dropped: ArgArray built = @('shell','am','start','','')→ after filter = @('shell','am','start')... wait Action=am, A1=start, A2="" because `-n` dropped entire rest? Then Run-Adb @('shell','am','start') → adb shell am start → "No intent supplied". Yes! That explains it.

Conclusion: I must invoke qa.ps1 in a way that passes `-n` and dashes literally. Options:
1. Use `--%` (stop parsing) — but then `&` operator with positional would... `--%` works only for native commands, not script calls.
2. Pass args as a SINGLE string in quotes: `& 'qa.ps1' 'am start -n com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'`? No — that changes positional binding (A1='am start -n ...') and the script would need string-splitting.
3. Add a dedicated `start` action in qa.ps1 that hardcodes nothing and passes everything literally: `qa.ps1 start` → internally Run-Adb @('shell','am','start','-n','com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'). Hardcode the component — ugly but reliable. Or:
4. Make qa.ps1 accept a raw passthrough: modify how bash tool calls it: instead of passing -n through the & operator, I'll quote each dashed arg in single quotes so PS passes them as literals! `& 'qa.ps1' am 'start' '-n' 'com.alarsheef.archive/.MainActivity'` — single-quoted strings are ALWAYS literals even if they start with `-`!! 

Wait, would that help? When PS assigns positional params, a quoted '-n' token is a value, not a parameter name token. YES. Quoting dashed args prevents parameter interpretation.

So the fix is at the CALL SITE: quote all args starting with `-` with single quotes in every invocation. That's error-prone across many calls. Better: change qa.ps1 to accept a NEW style: since every leading-dash token gets eaten, let me instead NOT pass device args through qa.ps1 params for the "am"/"sh" cases at all — have dedicated actions.

Actually simplest robust solution: **change the default action semantics of qa.ps1**: Make `Action` = first arg, and treat ALL remaining args as a literal list that I splice with "literal" semantics. PowerShell CAN'T avoid param-binding for script & invocation. BUT `-File` mode binds differently: with `-File`, PowerShell does NOT bind script parameters with param-name parsing! With `-File`, ALL args are positional?? No — earlier with -File, `-a` DID trigger "ambig between -Action -A1 -A2 -A3 -A4". That error came from qa.ps1's OWN param declaration seeing "-a"... no wait, that was from the bash tool's powershell -File invocation: `powershell -File qa.ps1 am start -a ...`. PowerShell -File DOES parse the args as script parameters (it binds by name). So same problem.

The real fix: **quote dashed tokens on invocation**. I'll always write them as '-n' in my call. That works via & operator AND -File? With -File: `-File qa.ps1 am '-n'` → binds A1='-n' as positional literal. Yes, quoting works for both.

Let me VERIFY by testing the quoted call before proceeding.

display.text:
package com.alarsheef.archive.scanner

import android.content.Context
import androidx.work.Constraints
import androidx.work.ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy
import androidx.work.ExistingWorkPolicy
import androidx.work.NetworkType
import androidx.work.OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder
import androidx.work.PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder
import androidx.work.WorkManager
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit

object WorkScheduler {

    fun scheduleDailyScan(context: Context) {
        val constraints = Constraints.Builder()
            .setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.NOT_REQUIRED)
            .build()

        val request = PeriodicWorkRequestBuilder<FileScannerWorker>(24, TimeUnit.HOURS)
            .setConstraints(constraints)
            .build()

        WorkManager.getInstance(context).enqueueUniquePeriodicWork(
            FileScannerWorker.UNIQUE_WORK_NAME,
            ExistingPeriodicWorkPolicy.KEEP,
            request
        )
    }

    fun cancelDailyScan(context: Context) {
        WorkManager.getInstance(context).cancelUniqueWork(FileScannerWorker.UNIQUE_WORK_NAME)
    }

    /** يشغّل فحصًا فوريًا لمرة واحدة (يُستخدم عند تفعيل الإعداد أول مرة، بدل انتظار 24 ساعة) */
    fun runOnce(context: Context) {
        val request = OneTimeWorkRequestBuilder<FileScannerWorker>().build()
        WorkManager.getInstance(context).enqueueUniqueWork(
            FileScannerWorker.ONE_TIME_WORK_NAME,
            ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP,
            request
        )
    }
}

42:         // بدون صلاحية الوصول للملفات لا فائدة من الفحص؛ ننهي بهدوء بدل
43:         // إعادة محاولة عبثية تستنزف البطارية (صلاحية مسحوبة لن تُحل بالتكرار)
44:         if (!PermissionUtils.hasStorageAccess(applicationContext)) return Result.success()
45: 
46:         return try {
47:             val repository = ArchiveRepository(applicationContext)
48:             val startedAt = System.currentTimeMillis()
49:             val lastScanAt = prefs.lastScanAt.first()
50: 
51:             val sources = buildList {
52:                 if (prefs.sourceWhatsapp.first()) add(SourceApp.WHATSAPP)
53:                 if (prefs.sourceGallery.first()) add(SourceApp.GALLERY)
54:                 if (prefs.sourceDownloads.first()) add(SourceApp.DOWNLOADS)
55:             }
56:             val excludePersonalPhotos = prefs.excludePersonalPhotos.first()
57: 
58:             for (source in sources) {

70:                 }
71:             }
72: 
73:             // مجلد الاستيراد المخصص (إن حُدّد عبر منتقي النظام)
74:             val customUri = prefs.importFolderUri.first()
75:             if (customUri != null) {
76:                 try {
77:                     scanCustomTree(

90:             }

92:             prefs.setLastScanAt(startedAt)
93:             // بعد فحص ناجح: نطلق التحليل الذكي للواردات الجديدة على الجهاز
94:             com.alarsheef.archive.work.AiAnalysisScheduler.start(applicationContext)

96:         } catch (e: IOException) {

98:             Result.retry()
99:         } catch (e: SecurityException) {
100:             // صلاحية سحبت أثناء الفحص — لا معنى لإعادة المحاولة
101:             Log.w(TAG, "فقدان صلاحية الوصول أثناء الفحص: ${e.message}")
102:             Result.failure()
103:         } catch (e: Throwable) {

109: 
110:     private suspend fun scanFolder(
111:         folder: File,
112:         source: SourceApp,
113:         repository: ArchiveRepository,
114:         excludePersonalPhotos: Boolean,
115:         lastScanAt: Long,
116:         depth: Int = 0
117:     ) {
118:         if (depth > MAX_DEPTH) return
119:         val entries = folder.listFiles() ?: return
120: 
121:         for (entry in entries) {
122:             currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()
123: 
124:             if (entry.isDirectory) {

178:      */

181:         source: SourceApp,
182:         repository: ArchiveRepository,
183:         excludePersonalPhotos: Boolean,
184:         lastScanAt: Long,
185:         depth: Int = 0

194:         source: SourceApp,

249:             } catch (e: SecurityException) {

251:             } catch (e: IOException) {
252:                 throw e
253:             } finally {
254:                 runCatching { temp.delete() }
255:             }

$dir = "$env:TEMP\opencode\qa_imgs"

function New-TestImage($name, $pathSuffix, $r, $g, $b, $date) {
    $path = Join-Path $dir $pathSuffix
    $bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap 160, 120
    $graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
    $graphics.Clear([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb(255, $r, $g, $b))
    $graphics.DrawString($name, (New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Arial', 14)), [System.Drawing.Brushes]::White, 10, 50)
    $ext = [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($path)
    $fmt = if ($ext -eq '.jpg') { [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Jpeg } else { [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png }
    $bmp.Save($path, $fmt)
    $graphics.Dispose(); $bmp.Dispose()
    [System.IO.File]::SetLastWriteTime($path, [DateTime]$date)
    Write-Output "created $pathSuffix (mtime $date)"
}

function New-TestImage($name, $pathSuffix, $red, $green, $blue, $date) {
    $path = Join-Path $dir $pathSuffix
    $bmp = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap 160, 120
    $graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bmp)
    $graphics.Clear([System.Drawing.Color]::FromArgb([int]255, [int]$red, [int]$green, [int]$blue))
    $graphics.DrawString([string]$name, (New-Object System.Drawing.Font('Arial', 14)), [System.Drawing.Brushes]::White, 10, 50)
    $ext = [System.IO.Path]::GetExtension($path)
    if ($ext -eq '.jpg') { $bmp.Save($path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Jpeg) }
    else { $bmp.Save($path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png) }
    $graphics.Dispose(); $bmp.Dispose()
    [System.IO.File]::SetLastWriteTime($path, [DateTime]::Parse($date))
    "created $pathSuffix (mtime $date)"
}

Workdir D:\Arsheef\alarsheef-v5. Long build — set timeout 600000. If the tool kills the wrapper, the build continues; but calling process waits... risk of timeout. Use Start-Process with redirect file then poll. Let me write a small runner: run gradlew via Start-Process -RedirectStandardOutput to log, -Wait. That worked for adb earlier issue? Start-Process had the -n arg problem but for plain arguments (no dashes) it works fine. gradlew args like :app:assembleDebug have no leading dash. Use Start-Process with -WindowStyle Hidden? -NoNewWindow. Log to file. Then read tail.

Actually simpler: just run directly `& .\gradlew.bat :app:assembleDebug > build.log 2>&1` in PowerShell via bash tool — the wrapper may get killed by tool but gradle continues in bg writing to log... but the redirected file handle then closes when the process is killed? If PowerShell host is killed, gradlew spawns gradle via java child — redirect handle attached to the killed process... messy. 

Better use Start-Process detach with redirect and poll. Let me create a generic run-gradle.ps1:
```
param($Task)
$env:JAVA_HOME='C:\Users\Me\.jdks\jdk-17.0.20.1+1'
$env:Path="$env:JAVA_HOME\bin;"+$env:Path
$log = "$env:TEMP\opencode\gradle_$Task.log"
Remove-Item $log -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Start-Process -FilePath ".\gradlew.bat" -ArgumentList @($Task, '--console=plain') -WorkingDirectory "D:\Arsheef\alarsheef-v5" -NoNewWindow -RedirectStandardOutput $log -RedirectStandardError "$log.err" -Wait
Get-Content $log -Tail 40
```
Hmm Start-Process with --console=plain (no dashes? "--console" has dashes!). That's like the -n problem for Start-Process ArgumentList? The -n problem earlier was actually the qa.ps1 param binding, NOT Start-Process! Wait — earlier I concluded Start-Process was fine and the issue was `& 'script.ps1' args` param binding. Actually re-examine: the FIRST Start-Process errors ("Cannot validate argument... null or empty") were due to empty-string elements in ArgumentList (my filter fixed that). The `-n` "No intent supplied" problem was in qa.ps1's param binding via & — NOT Start-Process. Direct `& $adb @a` worked. So Start-Process ArgumentList with dashed args is probably fine — the earlier am failure was a combination: (1) empty filter bug fixed, (2) `-n` eaten by & operator param binding in qa.ps1. Let me stop re-analyzing; the current qa.ps1 uses direct `&` invocation now and works.

For gradle, avoid dashed args entirely: use `--console=plain` → could cause issues; skip it, default console fine. Just `:app:assembleDebug`.

FOUND IT:
```
W PdfToImage: فشل تصيير الصفحة 0 من today_doc.pdf: Unsupported pixel format
```

`PdfRenderer.Page.render(bitmap, ...)` with `Bitmap.Config.RGB_565` fails with **"Unsupported pixel format"**. On Android, `PdfRenderer.Page.render()` REQUIRES `ARGB_8888` bitmap (or `RGBA_F16`/`RGB_565`? Actually the doc: render() requires ARGB_8888). Historically `render()` with RGB_565 throws. So the comment in the converter ("يُستخدم RGB_565 ...") is based on a wrong assumption — PdfRenderer demands ARGB_8888.

So this was a PRE-EXISTING BUG in PDF→PNG (every PDF page failed with "Unsupported pixel format"), before my same-day change. Now confirmed with the diagnostic logs. Fix: change `Bitmap.Config.RGB_565` → `ARGB_8888`. The memory justification in the comment flips — A4@400DPI ARGB_8888 ≈ 4 bytes/px. The pattern: when adb invokes `run-as pkg rm -f /path/*`, the REMOTE shell (which expands globs) is `sh -c "run-as pkg rm -f /path/*"`? No: `adb shell "cmd"` runs cmd via the device's shell `sh -c 'cmd'`. sh expands `/path/*` IF the directory is readable — run-as drops to app UID; listing /data/data/.../files should be same UID readable. Glob expansion happens in the OUTER sh before run-as? The outer sh is running as SHELL user (not app), which does NOT have permission to read /data/data/com.alarsheef.archive/files (SELinux). SELinux blocks shell from listing app private dir → glob fails to expand → `*` passed literally to rm → rm tries to delete literal `*` → gone as `-f` (no error). Then the INNER run-as... wait no, the command IS only run-as; the outer sh expands FIRST (fails: no glob match, leaves literal `*`), then runs `run-as ... rm -f <literal *>`. run-as as app UID: rm -f `*` → tries unlink literal `*` doesn't exist → -f ignore success. So DELETE NEVER actually worked.

Fix: avoid glob — run rm INSIDE run-as so the app UID lists its own dir. i.e. `adb shell run-as com.alarsheef.archive sh -c 'rm -f files/archive/2026/*/*/*'` — the inner sh (app UID) can read the dir and expand globs.
